summary: This RFC reproduces a letter from a Department of Defense official transmitting the National Research Council report on transport protocols and requesting specific actions on its recommendations. It was replaced by RFC 1039.

eli5.summary: A boss at the defense department sent the experts' report along with a note saying what should be done about it.

questions: what did the dod say about the nrc report
what did the dod say about transport protocols
subtitle: A DoD position on transport protocols from the National Research Council.

tldr.problem: The DoD received recommendations from the National Research Council on whether to use TCP/IP or a different international transport protocol standard.
tldr.mechanism: The DoD statement accepted the recommendation to adopt ISO TP-4 as a co-standard alongside TCP/IP, with plans to monitor TP's commercial availability and eventually move to it.
tldr.outcome: This was replaced by RFC 1039, which provided the actual NRC report and follow-up guidance.

today: RFC 945 is historic. It was replaced by RFC 1039, which contained the full NRC report and follow-up recommendations. The DoD ultimately standardized on TCP/IP, and ISO TP was never widely adopted.

sections.title: The Policy Statement
sections.content: RFC 945 reproduces a memo from the DoD Assistant Secretary of Defense stating the government's position on transport protocols. The memo acknowledges the National Research Council report that recommended adopting ISO TP-4 as a co-standard to TCP/IP, and directs the Defense Communications Agency to prepare for evaluating TP in commercial implementations.
sections.eli5: A boss shared the experts' advice with the people who manage computer networks and told them to get ready to test the new technology.

sections.title: The DoD Approach
sections.content: The DoD endorsed the idea of adopting ISO TP-4 as a co-standard to the existing TCP/IP standard. However, the memo recognized that TP was not yet a proven commercial offering, so the agency would monitor its progress, test it when implementations became available, and eventually transition to it if it proved suitable.
sections.eli5: The DoD agreed to try the new thing when it was ready, but they would keep using what worked in the meantime.

sections.title: Actions Requested
sections.content: The memo requested five specific actions from the Defense Communications Agency: develop military requirement specifications for TP, ensure DoD participation in commercial standards working groups, prepare the protocol test facility for TP testing, develop a transition strategy with resource estimates, and evaluate detailed recommendations from the NRC report.
sections.eli5: The memo asked for five things: write down what the DoD needs, stay involved in the standards process, get ready to test, plan the switch, and review the details.

references.text: National Research Council, "Transport Protocols for Department of Defense Data Networks", RFC 942, February 1985.
